answer_text:
Let  
\[
R=A_m=\left(\mathbb C[x,y]/(x^3-y^2)\right)_{(\bar x-1,\bar y-1)}
\]
and let \(I=mR\) be its maximal ideal. We want \(\mu_R(I)\), the minimal number of generators of \(I\) as an \(R\)-module.

By Nakayama’s lemma, since \(R\) is local with residue field
\[
R/I \cong A/m \cong \mathbb C,
\]
we have
\[
\mu_R(I)=\dim_{\mathbb C} I/I^2.
\]

Now set
\[
X=\bar x-1,\qquad Y=\bar y-1.
\]
Then \(I=(X,Y)R\). We need to understand the relations in \(I/I^2\).

Work in the regular local ring
\[
B=\mathbb C[x,y]_{(x-1,y-1)},\qquad \mathfrak n=(x-1,y-1)B.
\]
The relation in \(A\) is
\[
x^3-y^2=0.
\]
Substitute \(x=1+X\), \(y=1+Y\):
\[
(1+X)^3-(1+Y)^2
= 3X-2Y+3X^2+X^3-Y^2.
\]
Modulo \(\mathfrak n^2\), all terms of degree at least \(2\) vanish, so the relation in \(\mathfrak n/\mathfrak n^2\) is
\[
3X-2Y=0.
\]
Thus in \(I/I^2\),
\[
3X-2Y=0,
\]
or equivalently
\[
Y=\frac{3}{2}X.
\]
Therefore \(I/I^2\) is generated by the single class of \(X\), and it is nonzero. Hence
\[
\dim_{\mathbb C} I/I^2=1.
\]

By Nakayama’s lemma,
\[
\mu(mA_m)=1.
\]

\[
\boxed{1}
\]
